dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis intact on Sep 5 despite the surprise August NFP print (+162K vs +56K consensus, released Sep 4) which reversed rate-cut pricing to a 52% market-implied probability of a Sep 16 hike; 5 of 8 indicators remain supportive: Global M2 still expanding at $103.4T (4-week uptrend), 2s10s steepening to +40bps, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.73T, BTC funding near zero (+0.007%), and stablecoin dominance falling to 10.84% (from 11.31%) on a 30-day basis; DXY nudged up to 99.16 but holds in the neutral band; BTC.D at 56.58% (CMC methodology) remains above the 55% alt-rotation trigger, TOTAL stable at $2.82T; ECB decision (Sep 10) and FOMC (Sep 16) are the pivotal catalyst pair ahead.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); June 2026 confirmed at $102,663.81B ≈ $102.7T (MacroMicro); global broad money supply reached a record $150T in June 2026 (broader M3 measure per Crypto Briefing); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (29th consecutive monthly increase, +5.4% YoY, record high); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.7T → July estimate $103.4T = +$0.7T, well above flat threshold); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global aggregate not yet published; status supportive (4-week rising trend met); NFP surprise (+162K Sep 4) raises rate hike probability at FOMC Sep 16, which could slow the pace of global M2 expansion if the Fed tightens; ECB Sep 10 decision (expected hike) and FOMC Sep 16 are the next key catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 10:00 AM ET: 54.6%, down 1.0 percentage point from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); below 55.2% consensus; Production 58.3%, New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp vs July); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising, not met; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62, neither applies); strong August NFP (+162K, Sep 4) signals broad labor resilience despite the PMI softening; September ISM Manufacturing PMI (covering September activity) will be released October 1 — next reading; PMI at 54.6% corresponds to ~2.4% annualized real GDP growth.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.16 on September 4, 2026 (September 5 is a Saturday; Sep 4 close used; TradingEconomics/CNBC aggregates); 4-week trend down: from approximately 101.0–101.4 in early August 2026 (late-July peak ~101.40) to 99.16 Sep 4 = −1.8% relative decline, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; August NFP surprise (+162K vs +56K) on Sep 4 pushed DXY intraday to ~99.3 (post-NFP bounce per Schwab/Barchart) before settling at 99.16; 4-week trend remains DOWN despite the NFP bounce; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.16 within 97.5–100 neutral band); structural dollar weakness driven by Treasury buyback program offset by hawkish NFP repricing; markets now pricing ~52% chance of Sep 16 hike; a DXY break above 100 would shift status to headwind; a break below 97.5 would shift to supportive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.45% as of September 2, 2026 (MacroMicro/CNBC US10YTIP confirmed; FRED API blocked this run); Sep 4 data expected to be slightly higher after strong NFP (+162K vs +56K), which pushed nominal 10Y yields from 4.754% to ~4.79% (+3.6bps); breakeven inflation likely flat, implying Sep 4 real yield ~2.47–2.49% — unconfirmed, held at 2.45% per last verified observation; 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% (Aug 4 estimate) → 2.45% (Sep 2) = +2bps, within the 5bps flat threshold; status neutral (flat 4-week trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition is not fully triggered; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met); 10-year TIPS auction Jul 23 cleared at 2.438% real; CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16 are next catalysts for TIPS yield direction.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 4, 2026: pre-NFP 10Y yield 4.7541%, 2Y yield 4.3390% (CNBC/Treasury); post-NFP 10Y rose ~3.6bps to 4.79%; 2Y rose more sharply on rate-hike repricing (markets pricing ~52% Sep 16 hike after +162K NFP vs +56K consensus); estimated post-NFP spread: 10Y 4.79% minus 2Y ~4.39% ≈ +40bps (+0.40%); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 4 estimate per prior run) → +40bps (Sep 4) = +5bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; spread above zero well outside the −50bps headwind threshold); FRED DGS10/DGS2 proxy-blocked this run — values sourced from secondary CNBC/web search aggregates; curve-shaping events: ECB Sep 10 (expected +25bps hike), CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16; a Sep 16 hike (vs expected cut) would likely flatten the curve as 2Y rises faster than 10Y.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.73T for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27; latest available); H.4.1 for week ending September 3, 2026 scheduled for release September 10, 2026 at 4:30 PM ET (source: Fed H.4.1 calendar); prior Aug 19 H.4.1 confirmed $6.7T (search aggregate); 4-week trend flat: $6.70T (Aug 19) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = +$30B, within flat threshold; routine measured QT continues (MBS runoff; Treasury reinvestment maintains stability); status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no QT acceleration, no overnight rate spike); FRED WALCL API blocked this run; next confirmed WALCL read (Sep 3 week) arrives Sep 10 alongside ECB decision and PPI — watch for any balance sheet policy guidance in FOMC Sep 16 statement.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.007% per 8h (Sep 4, 2026 observation carried forward; CoinGlass blocked Sep 5 — egress proxy denial); BTC price pulled back from $81,044 (Sep 4 NFP day) to $79,581 (Sep 5 Saturday crypto market; CoinMarketCap); a ~1.8% BTC pullback on strong NFP (rate hike fears) typically produces neutral-to-flat funding, consistent with +0.007% remaining near zero; 30-day trend flat: near zero or slightly negative throughout August 2026, slightly positive at +0.007% since Sep 4; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action, no leveraged long accumulation); BTC.D: 56.58% per CoinMarketCap (Sep 5); TOTAL crypto market cap $2.82T (Sep 5, stable); alt-rotation trigger not met (BTC.D > 55%).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$306B (Sep 5, 2026; CoinGecko/CryptoRank.io aggregates); total crypto market cap $2.82T (CoinMarketCap Sep 5); stablecoin dominance 10.84% ($306B / $2.82T); down from 11.31% (Sep 4 run) and ~13–14% in early August 2026; 30-day trend down: sustained ~2–3pp decline over 30 days reflecting capital deployment from stablecoins into risk assets predominantly Bitcoin; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL also rising — does not apply as TOTAL is roughly flat at $2.82T); BTC.D at 56.58% (CoinMarketCap methodology, includes stablecoins in denominator; prior BeInCrypto/AMBCrypto 60%+ reading used a narrower denominator excluding stablecoins); alt-rotation trigger (BTC.D sub-55% sustained) not met on either methodology; USDT market share 60.82% of all stablecoins (USDT $186B + USDC $70B ≈ 82% combined).

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—pipeline inflation read one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC Sep 16; July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%; per BLS archive); August NFP surprise (+162K vs +56K, Sep 4) has reset rate expectations to ~52% probability of a Sep 16 hike; a hot PPI print would strengthen the case for a hike and could pressure risk assets; a cooling PPI would add to disinflationary narrative and reduce hike probability heading into CPI Sep 11; released same day as ECB rate decision (Sep 10) and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6, 2026—labor read released the same day as PPI and ECB decision; week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000; strong August NFP (+162K) confirmed labor market resilience on Sep 4; a spike in claims above 220K would temper the new rate-hike narrative heading into CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16; released alongside PPI August and ECB rate decision, making Sep 10 a triple-event day.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET; Reuters poll (Sep 3, 2026) showed 65 economists expecting the ECB to HIKE the deposit rate by 25bps to 2.50%; an ECB hike released the same day as US PPI and US jobless claims would reinforce global rate-hike narrative and could push DXY back above 100 (headwind threshold) if combined with a hot PPI; strong US NFP (+162K, Sep 4) already shifted markets to 52% probability of a Sep 16 Fed hike—concurrent ECB and Fed tightening would be a significant headwind for risk assets near-term; ECB guidance on future pace of tightening and inflation forecasts will be closely watched.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; the data trifecta is now: NFP Sep 4 (+162K, strong), CPI Sep 11, then FOMC Sep 16; markets pricing 52% probability of a hike after NFP beat; a hot CPI above 3.8% YoY would likely lock in a Sep 16 hike and trigger DXY above 100 (headwind for risk assets); a soft CPI below 3.3% would pull back hike expectations and support risk assets even after the strong NFP; PCE inflation for July 2026 was 3.7% YoY (released Aug 26); includes core CPI ex-food and energy; the Fed-ECB divergence risk is maximal if ECB hikes Sep 10 while US CPI cools Sep 11.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—released same day as CPI August; captures consumer inflation expectations (1-year and 5-year) alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; if the NFP surprise (+162K, Sep 4) boosts consumer confidence but also raises inflation expectations, the Fed faces a stagflation-adjacent optics problem; elevated 1-year inflation expectations alongside hot CPI would strengthen the case for a Sep 16 hike; a drop in confidence alongside cooling CPI would temper hike odds and create a risk-asset supportive setup heading into FOMC.
